articleTitle: Development of an Reliable SHM System for Damage Monitoring of Railway Axles using FPGAs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) is an effective tool for ensuring integrity and safety, capable of detecting damage with high precision. The computing architecture of Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs) allows for programmable and reconfigurable hardware, offering flexibility and adaptability. Combining the real-time, low-latency computational capabilities of FPGAs with SHM systems represents a promising approach in safety-critical embedded systems. This paper proposes an ultrasonic-based SHM system for monitoring damage in railway axles using FPGAs. The proposed SHM system includes a hardware trigger mechanism that uses an incremental encoder to initiate measurements at specific angular positions of the axle. Additionally, a data transfer system will be designed and implemented to reliably transfer measurement and meta data to the system's memory in real-time. The individual hardware components of the proposed system have been simulated using Xilinx Vivado, and the complete hardware system has been evaluated using Zynq 7020 System-on-Chip (SoC) FPGA board. While the system is specifically designed for monitoring railway axles, it can also be applied to other types of axles.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of Full Authority Digital Electronic Control System Based on Multi-state Binary Decision Diagram
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: To efficiently assess the probabilistic safety of full authority digital electronic control system within aeroengine, a system reliability model was established, using the loss of thrust control as the boundary condition. A probabilistic safety assessment method based on a multi-state binary decision diagram was proposed and subsequently verified through case simulation. For the multi-state of full authority digital electronic control system, an analysis was conducted to identify the system units that contribute to the occurrence of multi-state events, leading to the establishment of a reliability model for the system. A multi-state fault tree was generated, with the loss of thrust control designated as the top event, and this fault tree was analyzed in depth. The method involved prioritizing traversal and constructing a multi-state binary decision diagram model for probabilistic safety assessment, allowing for the calculation of the probability expression for each state of the system. Engineering cases were presented, and MATLAB simulation analysis was employed to obtain the probability curves of each state of the system at various times (t), thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results indicate that this evaluation method can rapidly compute the probabilities of system states across all levels using mathematical expressions, addressing the challenges of low computational efficiency and the limitations of traditional reliability analysis methods, which are typically confined to small models. This approach can be applied to aerospace engine electronics with n sensors in the control system.

articleTitle: System Belief Reliability Evaluation Method Based on Uncertainty Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: On the basis of probability theory, fitting data based on the law of large numbers can quickly obtain the distribution or variation patterns of data. However, in the system design phase, the system has not yet been put into use, and reliability cannot be analyzed through statistical fault data. The performance data of various functions and modules in the design phase is also relatively limited. In this case, directly using probability theory methods to fit the data would result in significant cognitive uncertainty. Therefore, this article proposes a method for analyzing the reliability of test data from the perspective of functional performance, based on uncertainty theory. This method collects data on key parameters of the system and fits their distribution and two factor degradation patterns. From the perspective of functional margin, it establishes disciplinary equations for performance parameters and injects the distribution and degradation patterns of key parameters to conduct reliable analysis. This article takes integrated operational amplification circuits as a case study to compare the analysis results based on uncertainty theory and probability theory. The results indicate that in the case of limited data, uncertainty theory can better describe cognitive uncertainty in fitting, and reliability analysis results are more conservative.

articleTitle: Single Point of Failure Assessment Case Study for Bulk Plant Electrical System Saudi Aramco
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Single Point of Failure (SPoF) equipment is defined as any asset that if failed, it will cause an interruption on the entire facility or single product supply/receive operation. The study aims to present the result of the evaluation of all electrical equipment that meets the SPoF definition, evaluate the current available mitigation measures, and then provide recommendations as applicable to have Saudi Aramco facilities and systems robust, self-sustained, and reliable. Single Point of Failure Assessment is an assessment that was conducted in order to evaluate all electrical equipment that meet the SPoF definition, evaluate the current available mitigation measures, and then provide applicable recommendations to have facilities and systems robust, self-sustained, and reliable. In addition, a Single Point of Failure Assessment will be conducted in the future for the mechanical systems at Bulk Plant Facilities

articleTitle: A Robust Modeling Method for Uncertainty Convex Polyhedron Models Based on Outlier Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Accurate quantification of uncertainty is a prerequisite for achieving reliable structural design. The convex polyhedron model, which considers correlations between variables, is a non-probabilistic method for quantifying uncertainty. However, when significant outliers are present, the convex hull constructed by the convex polyhedron method can become distorted and stretched, affecting the model's predictive capability for future samples. This paper proposes a robust convex polyhedron modeling method based on outlier detection, which is insensitive to outliers in the sample set. First, outlier detection algorithms are used to exclude outliers from the sample points. Then, a convex polyhedron model is constructed based on the remaining sample points, and an expansion factor is defined to ensure that the volume of the new convex hull is the same as that of the original convex hull, thereby maintaining the new model's predictive capability. An engineering example demonstrates the superiority of this modeling method in the presence of outliers.

articleTitle: Model Based Fault Management and Isolation Algorithm Design Integrated with Micro Service Architecture (Remİks)
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: A method used for fault management and localization in military systems is presented. Fault localization, the process of determining the approximate location of a fault, is a key component of this method. The method utilizes the fault propagation behaviour of the system and power supply interfaces within the system items for fault isolation purposes. Fault isolation, which involves determining the location of a fault to the extent necessary to effect repair, is crucial for effective maintenance. In addition to this, special fault scenarios are introduced to the fault management algorithm to handle various system fault evaluation scenarios. The fault diagnosis findings, the faulty items and derived Built-in tests (BIT) results, of the algorithm are demonstrated on user interface for the maintenance personnel or operator to initiate appropriate corrective actions.

articleTitle: Combining Security and Safety Engineering with Formal Verification to Improve Reliability of Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The consideration of safety and security assessments in robotic systems is increasingly crucial due to their inherent interdependence. Incorrectly configured or improperly deployed systems become vulnerable to security threats, which can directly impact safety. Given that security vulnerabilities often lead to safety hazards, identifying and mitigating potential vulnerabilities becomes essential for maintaining overall safety. In this paper, we propose a model-based approach specifically tailored to industrial robotics. Our approach integrates safety and security engineering with formal verification techniques to ensure the reliability of robotic systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a practical case study in the manufacturing robotics domain, emphasizing how safety and security concerns align with traditional system design and analysis phases.

articleTitle: A Sample Synthesis Method for Railway Track Circuit Fault Diagnosis Based on Variational Autoencoder and Improved SMOTEENN
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Accurately identifying fault modes in track circuits is crucial for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the equipment. However, in practical diagnostic processes, there is often an imbalance problem where the number of faulty samples is significantly smaller than the number of normal samples. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sample synthesis technique that combines variational autoencoder (VAE) with an improved synthetic minority over-sampling technique edited nearest neighbor (SMOTEENN). At first, VAE is employed to thoroughly extract features from the raw monitoring data. The VAE-encoded data is, then, subjected to hybrid sampling using the SMOTEENN algorithm. Next, a filtering method based on the Chebyshev distance is proposed to further improve the quality of the synthesized samples. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using a track circuit simulation dataset. The experimental results demonstrate that the synthesis method proposed in this paper significantly enhances the accuracy of fault diagnosis compared to the SMOTE, SMOTEENN and VAE-SMOTEENN methods.

articleTitle: Fatigue Life Prediction Method with Multi-Stress-Ratio Sparse Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Rational characterization and quantification of un-certainty are key to fatigue life prediction. And multi-stress ratio sparse fatigue data introduce further effects of epistemic uncertainty to the quantitative characterization of uncertainty. Thus, in this paper, the survival a - s - <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> curves are firstly defined to express the uncertainty in the relationship of stress level and fatigue life, and the expression for the multi-stress-ratio condition is also clarified. Then the parameter estimation process are established suiting for uncertainty quantification with the sparse fatigue life data. Finally, a case study is used to show the effectiveness of the proposed model and method in the fatigue life prediction with multi-stress-ratio sparse data.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation Method for Parallel Mechanisms Kinematics under Time-Varying Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Under the action of time-varying dynamic loads, the deformation caused by the degradation of the linkage stiffness in parallel mechanisms and the deformation caused by impact responses are coupled, resulting in high uncertainty that reduces motion stability and accuracy. This paper proposes a motion reliability evaluation method that considers the propagation of epistemic uncertainty. The uncertain Liu process is employed to model the uncertain degradation process of key connecting components in parallel mechanisms. The inverse uncertainty distribution is utilized in both forward and inverse kinematics models to calculate the impact of structural degradation on kinematics reliability. In the case study involving a humanoid robot's ankle joint, the proposed reliability evaluation method is compared with a probability-based approach. The results indicate that the proposed method would provide a more conservative maintenance strategy.

articleTitle: Diversification in Collective Water Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The theme of the publication is to provide a method of determining the diversification degree of water resources in collective water supply systems. For the purposes of the method Shannon-Weaver indicator was adapted. The paper presents a method of two-parameter assessment of water resources diversification with the proposal of collective water supply systems categorization of the diversification degree. The method takes into account the water intakes of and network water tanks. The number of water intakes and their share in the total supply for collective water supply systems, as well as the number and volume of network water tanks allows to calculate the dimensionless diversification ratios and to compare different collective water supply systems.

articleTitle: A Nonlocal Stress/Strain Correction Method of Notched Areas for Turbine Blades Service Life Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: A nonlocal stress/strain approximation correction method based on Neuber's rule is proposed to achieve plastic correction of the linear elastic stress/strain state along the crack propagation path in the critical plane by ensuring the premise of force and moment balance. The method can quickly obtain the local stress and strain of the turbine blade notch during use. Based on the proposed method, combined with the low cycle fatigue (LCF) life prediction method based on the critical plane-critical distance, the LCF life of the notched part of the turbine blade can be predicted more accurately. The proposed method was validated using structural nonlinear finite element analysis (FEA) and experimental results for the blade tenon specimens subjected to LCF load. The comparison of computed and analyzed stress/strain revealed a good agreement. All predicted life values fall within a 3-factor scatter band when compared with the experimental life data.

articleTitle: A Virtual Data-Driven Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Adaptive Regularisation Consistency
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The success of traditional fault diagnosis methods depends on obtaining a large number of training samples in the form of full faults, which may not be available in practical applications. Recent studies have shown the feasibility of constructing virtual representations reacting to fault situations by building physical models when fault samples are insufficient. In this paper, a virtual data-driven domain-based adaptive fault diagnosis method based on adaptive regularisation consistency, ARC, is proposed to ensure the consistency between the virtual and real domains. Firstly, the bearing dynamic model is constructed to obtain the simulation data, and the simulation data and the real data are input into the trained original model and the target model at the same time. The data distributions of the simulated and real samples are adaptively brought closer by adding weights to the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD); Kullback-Leibler Divergence (KLD) is used to make the feature representations extracted from the target model similar to each other and between the original model and the feature representations extracted from the target model, and regularization is used to fine-tune the feature extraction of the model. An entropy-based adaptive pseudo-labelling selection method is proposed to filter low-quality samples and prevent negative transfer. The diagnostic results of the case study show that the proposed method is able to utilize the diagnostic knowledge from the simulation data to achieve fault diagnosis of mechanical equipment and outperforms the commonly used unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis methods.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis Study of Multi-Scenario Fire Accidents for Oil Storage Tank Area
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Oil storage tank area has a large centralized storage capacity, and due to its flammable and explosive nature, it is susceptible to a variety of fire accidents during the production, storage and transportation process. In order to better assess the accident risk level of petrochemical enterprises and take matching and effective emergency measures, a more accurate risk assessment model is constructed based on the Bayesian network. The chain development process of accident spatio-temporal evolution based on domino effect is considered, and the probability and consequence of 8 accident types are summarized and refined. The results show that the emergence of the domino effect leads to an increase in the accident risk value by a factor of 15.7 to 63.9 compared with the fire risk assessment of a single storage tank. The method can effectively improve the accuracy of the multi-scenario accident risk assessment system for storage tank clusters and improve the safety management level of petrochemical enterprises.

articleTitle: ARtificial Intelligence and STOchasTic Simulation for the rEsiLience of Critical InfrastructurES (ARISTOTELES)
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In this paper, we present the ambitions of the research project ARtificial Intelligence and STOchasTic simulation for the rEsiLience of critical infrastructurES (ARISTOTELES), funded by the Italian Ministry for Scientific Research (MIUR) under the PRIN 2022 program (grant 2022TAFXZ5) and by the European Union - Next Generation EU program. The aim is to share the objectives and preliminary results, for fostering further collaboration.

articleTitle: Distribution of Error and Performance Rates to Sensors in the Scenario-Driven Development of Autonomous Vehicles to Determine Acceptable Error Rates and Estimate the Remaining Risk
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Efficient allocation of performance and error rate budgets in the development of autonomous and intelligent vehicles is paramount for ensuring both Functional Safety (ISO 26262) and Safety of the Intended Functionality (SOTIF) (ISO 21448). This paper delves into the approach of distributing performance and error rate budgets to functional scenarios, considering the stringent safety requirements outlined in these standards. First scenarios are analyzed and categorized using the functional Safety (FuSa) risk classes. In doing so, the allocation of error rate budgets to identify and mitigate potential hazards can be done effectively. As autonomous vehicles make use of a large set of sensors, it is necessary to further break down the error and performance rate requirements to specific sensors. Depending on the scenario the vehicle is encountering, the position and type of the sensor for example plays a role for the contribution to the decision making of the following behavior of the vehicle. In this paper we present a method how to break down the overall performance rates to individual sensors. We present, moreover, how a performance model for an individual sensor is created and used along with the systematic derivation of individual performance rates. The systematic approach contributes to optimizing Autonomous Driving Systems (ADS) in vehicles for correct and anticipatory perception of the environment in the relevant scenarios. We present how the functional risk and overall risk of the active ADS in a defined scenario selection can be estimated. Therefore, it facilitates that the vehicle equipped with a complex ADS will be developed, validated and released compliant with safety standards in its intended operational design domain (ODD).

articleTitle: DfR of the Grill Oven Relay
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper presents the application of the Design for Reliability (DfR) approach to the relay controlling the oven's grill heating element. The conventional stress-versus-strength reliability methodology is enhanced through data from connected devices and localized load measurements, enabling the derivation of a detailed load spectrum for the relay. This approach increases the accuracy of reliability predictions, eliminating the need for success-run tests typical of the test-to-pass approach.

articleTitle: Exploration of the Changes and Influence Patterns of Oil Contaminants in Hydraulic Components
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The hydraulic system in CNC machine tools is a critical subsystem that ensures the overall reliability of the machine. By utilizing a test bench that simulates the operation of the CNC machine tool hydraulic system, the correlation between environmental factors, the quantity of oil contaminants, and system failures is analyzed. A BP neural network is used to establish a model of the impact of environmental factors on oil contaminants in the CNC machine tool hydraulic system. The correlation of the impact of environmental factors on oil contaminants is determined through range analysis. Experiments are designed to explore the relationship between the concentration and size of solid contaminants in the oil and the working state of the hydraulic system. A BP neural network is used to establish a model of the impact of solid contaminants on the hydraulic system. The influence of environmental factors and contaminant factors on the reliability of the hydraulic system is investigated.

articleTitle: A Classification Problem Formulation for the Reliability Assessment of End-to-End Communication Among Cyber Devices of Cyber-Physical Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Telecommunication Networks (TLCNs) enable the control of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs). Reliable End-to-End (E2E) communication among TLCN devices is fundamental to prevent CPS failures. Simulating the complex underlying phenomena that cause E2E communication failure, such as transmission delays and package dropouts, might be computationally expensive, challenging the reliability assessment of E2E communication. To tackle this issue, we reframe the E2E communication as a classification problem to streamline its reliability assessment. We use Gradient Boosting (GB) as an example of an off-the-shelf classifier that can be tailored to the purpose of estimating the E2E communication success or failure, without relying on the long-running simulation of the information processing through the nodes of a TLCN embedded into a CPS. The CPS considered as case study is an Integrated Power and Telecommunication Network (IP&TLCN) system.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Applications in Internal Transportation Systems Maintenance: A Conceptual Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The article focuses on implementing the digital twin (DT) concept for mobile robot maintenance management. A digital twin is a virtual representation of a connected physical asset and gives the capability to predict its conditions in the future. As a result, the introduction of digital twins in any technical system, e.g., an internal transportation system, gives the possibility to decrease the volume of resources needed to design, produce, and keep transportation assets in a good operational state. Therefore, the main problem addressed in the paper is developing a framework for DT concept implementation in the maintenance management area of internal transportation systems. Indeed, the paper presents a short literature review on the defined research area. Later, the maintenance management problems of internal transportation systems are characterized. Based on this, the framework for DT concept implementation is presented. The work ends with conclusions and directions for further research.

articleTitle: Resilience of the Water Supply System to a Crisis Situation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The occurrence of a crisis situation may be caused by the forces of nature or have an anthropogenic background. These factors pose a threat to the functioning of various technical systems used by people, which can be also a threat to their health or life. One of the most important systems used by people is the collective water supply system (CWSS). Unlimited access to clean and safe water determines the development of citizens. Water supply companies should be prepared to supply water also during a crisis situation. The paper presents a method for assessing the resilience of CWSS to crisis situations in the aspect of water supply. The analysis covered ten water supply companies located in Poland. The results indicated significant shortcomings in the preparation of companies to ensure water supply in a crisis situation. Possible directions of development for the examined CWSS were indicated in order to increase the resilience of the system in the aspect of water supply during a crisis situation.

articleTitle: Improving Anomaly Detection with Adaptive Dynamic Threshold: A Review and Enhanced Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In fast-growing modern cyber-physical systems, reliability plays a vital role. Effective anomaly detection, which identifies security and safety issues at early stage, is essential for ensuring system reliability. While much research has focused on anomaly detection techniques, fewer studies address a key challenge, setting precise and responsive thresholds for anomaly detection. In this study, we conduct a comprehensive review of current threshold setting methods. Thereafter, we introduce a novel approach for adaptive threshold setting. Our method is tailored for diverse safety and security tasks and is tested on a safety-critical exoskeleton model and a cybersecurity scenario for energy systems. The results demonstrate that our approach could enhance the threshold setting for anomaly detection in CPS.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Applications for Reliable Fault Detection in Power Transformer Windings
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the localization of radial faults in power transformer windings using electromagnetic waves, emphasizing the critical issues of reliability and noise. The proposed analytical method aims to enhance the reliability of power transformers by effectively identifying and diagnosing radial deformations. The study utilizes matched filtering techniques to analyze received signals, ensuring improved accuracy despite environmental noise interference. By comparing the reference signals from healthy transformers with those from faulty conditions, the methodology demonstrates a robust framework for real-time monitoring. The findings indicate that addressing noise and reliability significantly contributes to the effectiveness of fault detection systems in power transformers.

articleTitle: Inoperability Assessment of Interdependent Critical Infrastructures by Minimal Inoperability Sets Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: We consider the inoperability assessment of two Critical Infrastructures (CIs), one dependent on the other. Typically, such inoperability assessment is conducted by generating failures in the ‘source’ CI and modeling the disruption cascade into the dependent CI. In realistically large CIs, this results in the need of exploring a combinatorial number of accidental scenarios, which becomes infeasible due to the computational burden. In this paper, a novel approach is presented to address the computational issue, which allows identifying the Minimal Inoperability Sets (MISs), i.e., the minimal combinations of failures leading the dependent CI into a partial or fully inoperability state to exhaustively explore the accidental scenarios. A case study of a power CI feeding a water CI is considered.

articleTitle: Interpretable Anomalous Event Detection with Uniform Dynamic Alignment of Time Series in Aircraft Aviation Safety
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Interpretable anomalous event detection plays a crucial role in proactive aviation safety by identifying anomalous patterns and explaining the occurrence of such events. However, varied-length time series in certain flight phases pose challenges for traditional modeling methods that require equal-length in-puts. To address this, we propose a uniform dynamic time warping with a uniform Scaling alignment method. This method combines global and local information, resolving the variable-length issue while minimizing information loss. Additionally, we perform error analysis on specific samples tot est t he detection model's capacity to identify different adverse samples with varied anomalous behaviors. Results in real flight data verify the proposed alignment method enhances the model performance and also shows a slight edge over other alignment methods.

articleTitle: Mitigating Risks in Renewable Energy Power Systems: Predicting Transient Voltage Angles with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: As the penetration of renewable energy in global power systems continues to increase, new challenges to the stability and reliability of these systems have emerged. This study focuses on the dynamic impact of wind power generation's uncertainty and variability on power systems under gusty conditions characterized by significant short-term wind speed fluctuations. This study employs Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to predict transient voltage angle variations in power systems subjected to wind power generation uncertainty. Using the IEEE 9 BUS system as a case study, voltage angle variations are generated through the swing equation and an ODE solver, serving as training data for the PINNs. The results demonstrate that PINNs effectively predicts transient voltage angles in unseen wind power datasets with only 20 training wind scenarios dataset. Overall, this paper illustrates the potential of PINNs in handling the complex dynamics of renewable energy-integrated power systems, particularly in forecasting and managing grid fluctuations caused by wind power generation.

articleTitle: Turnaround Maintenance Projects in the Petrochemical Industry: A Bibliometric Review of Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This study provides a review of the current state of research on TAM projects in the petrochemical industry, identifying key contributors, active publication sources, and challenges that need to be addressed for successful project execution. Utilizing R Studio software, bibliometric and content analysis were conducted on 63 research papers published between 2004 and 2024. The study identifies key challenges, including the need for improved risk management, enhanced collaboration among multidisciplinary teams, and the integration of advanced technologies. The results indicated the management of the shutdown process, risk management during the shutdown process and the resources intensive tasks as integral to TAM projects. This review highlights the need for ongoing research to address existing gaps and drive innovation in TAM practices, ultimately aiming to optimize maintenance strategies, improve operational safety, and ensure the long-term sustainability of the petrochemical industry.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Bayesian Network for the Performance Assessment of Nuclear Waste Repositories Undergoing Chemical Degradation due to Climate Change
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Concrete is used as a barrier to prevent the release of radioactive contaminants from nuclear waste repositories. Concrete suffers of two main chemical degradation processes that can be expedited by climate change: carbonation-induced corrosion and chloride ingress. In this work, a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN) is developed for evaluating the concrete degradation induced by variations in climatic factors that affect corrosion, e.g., temperature, relative humidity and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The DBN is applied with reference to near-surface waste disposal of literature, in support to the assessment of the risk of aquifer contamination due to radioactive contaminants release.

articleTitle: A PCI Express Based Data Acquisition System for the Monitoring of Code Traces of RISC-V Microprocessors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In the digital world cyberattacks represent a serious threat that can compromise vulnerable systems. Microprocessors, in particular, are exposed to a wide number of cyberattacks, such as Spectre and Meltdown based attacks, as well as Code-Reuse Attacks. In this paper, a PCI express (PCIe) based data acquisition (DAQ) system was developed to acquire the code traces of a RISC-V microprocessor. The code traces dataset will be used to design a machine learning based system on FPGA for on-line detection of cyberattacks in RISC-V microprocessors. The DAQ system was designed in Verilog HDL for Xilinx FPGA platforms and interfaced with a PC running Linux to acquire the code traces and to save them on the hard disk. In the current stage of development, the DAQ system performance was evaluated by generating controlled code traces of 512 bit with frequency 50 MHz using an ad-hoc developed digital circuit. Tests were carried out on two different FPGA platforms and for three different sizes of the SRAM memory buffer (64 kB, 512 kB and 4 MB). The results have shown that the latency introduced by the PC operating system can seriously impact the data transfer rate, and the maximum achieved data throughput was found 577.17 MB/s in the case of SRAM memory size of 4 MB.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hyperparameters of ResNet50 for 3t2FTS-based Tumor Grading
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) MR imaging allows for a comprehensive assessment of crucial factors like brain tumor volume and location. Also, two-dimensional (2D) analysis comprises more methods than 3D-based analysis to be applied for tumor classification, e.g. high-grade glioma (HGG) vs low-grade glioma (LGG). Regarding this, to accurately classify between HGG and LGG glioma types, each slice of 3D MR images can be analyzed using 3D to 2D feature transformation methods. In this paper, we utilize optimized-ResNet50 models to accurately classify 2D identity information (2D-ID) of HGG-and LGG-typed tumors that is the output of a 3D to 2D feature transformation strategy (3t2FTS). At this point, state-of-the-art algorithms including crystal structure algorithm (CSA), chaotic dynamic weight-particle swarm optimization (CDW-PSO), and modified social group optimization (MSGO) are compared to tune the hyperparameters of ResNet50, i.e. continuous & discrete optimization problem. The experimental results indicate that the ResNet50-CSA model achieves the highest accuracy (91.23%) on the 3t2FTS-based data. Furthermore, ResNet50-MSGO provides 87.72 % accuracy, and its operation time is nearly half of the time belonging to ResNet50-CSA. As a result, MSGO and especially CSA, demonstrate significant performance to catch a tradeoff between searching capacity (convergence capability), accuracy and operation time.

articleTitle: UAV Swarm Availability Analysis Based on Binary-State Systems and Multi-State Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is rapidly increasing. Certain tasks necessitate the deployment of multiple UAVs for a unified mission, forming what is known as a UAV swarm. A critical factor in assessing a UAV or UAV swarm is reliability. Various mathematical models are employed to analyze reliability. For instance, Binary-State Systems (BSS) models evaluate two states: operational/functional and faulty. Some research advocates for the use of a Multi-State System (MSS) model. MSS enables the examination of more than just two states (operational and faulty), providing a more comprehensive analysis. This paper presents a comparative study on calculating the availability of a UAV swarm using both BSS and MSS models. Different UAV swarm topologies are interpreted as typical MSS structures (series, parallel, k-out-of-n) and represented by structure function. The analysis includes both homogeneous and heterogeneous UAV swarms, which can be either non-redundant or redundant hot stable systems.

articleTitle: Reliable Blockchain-Based KYC Model for Blacklist Records in Insurance
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Know Your Customer (KYC), which is primarily utilized by banks in the financial system, improves financial organizations' processes. The information received from the customer throughout the KYC process can be utilized to prevent fraud, money laundering, and other illegal acts. KYC processes can be carried either by individual financial institutions or through a centralized system. Aside from both of these possibilities, it is also possible to conduct KYC processes using a blockchain-based system. In this study, insurance fraud records, which insurance companies call blacklists, are carried out with blockchain technology. The solution prepared on the Ethereum network allows different insurance companies to access the network and read and write blacklist records. Keeping a blacklist record, which can be associated as a KYC process, reveals a fast, unchangeable and transparent structure between insurance companies. The study also addresses methods to mitigate a critical vulnerability in these networks where a single actor can manipulate the system through fake identities. This situation is considered as a Sybil attack. The closing remarks underlines the eagerness of emerging regulations and standards for privacy, access control, data sharing, scalability, etc.

articleTitle: Asset Management Strategies for District Heating Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: District Heating (DH) became widely adopted in European cities during the 20th century to meet demand for heating from a growing urban population. Today, the desire to decarbonize Europe's heat consumption has lead to an renewed interest in increasing the adoption of DH. To meet this end, DH has to be a price competitive alternative to other heating technologies. Over time the underground heat distribution network that DH companies operate suffers from faults that require replacement of pipes. On-demand replacement is more expensive than planned large scale replacement projects. The only question is, when is the optimal time to renew the pipes? In this article this question will be formulated using Reliability Theory. Our approach is to use historical records of time to failure and a bounding result to estimate the optimal time for replacement. The method can be used by DH companies with historical fault records to form an Asset Management strategy on the question of when to renew which pipes.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SIMPRA) of Integrated Road-Power Infrastructures Travelled by EVs and ICVs
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The integration of road and power infrastructures with hybrid fleets of Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Internal Combustion Vehicles (ICVs) is considered. The Simulation-Based Probabilistic Risk Assessment (SIMPRA) method is used to explore failure scenarios which may arise in the integrated system. SIMPRA is made of the simulator, the scheduler and the planner. The planner models the engineering knowledge of the system by means of an Event Sequence Diagram (ESD); the scheduler aims to adaptively guide the simulation through the ESD finding the failure scenarios, ultimately simulated with the simulator. SIMPRA is applied to a road infrastructure in the New York State, traveled by a blended fleet of EVs and ICVs (with different EVs penetration levels). An IEEE 14 buses power infrastructure is integrated with the road infrastructure for satisfying the energy demand of the EVs. Accidental scenarios of different magnitudes are considered. The results show the capability of SIMPRA of identifying the events that bear the largest vehicle travel times and delays, i.e., the events exposing most to disruptions the road-power infrastructure.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lubrication Characteristics of Electric Spindle Bearings
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: During the operation of the electric spindle, the spindle bearings undergo high-speed rotation, and good lubrication conditions are crucial. Poor lubrication can cause bearing contact fatigue, frictional damage, spindle abnormal noise, excessive vibration, spindle seizure, and other failures. Angular contact ball bearings are commonly used in electric spindle bearings, and lubrication is often achieved through grease lubrication. This study focuses on the analysis of the kinematic relationship of the 7009AC angular contact ball bearing under load conditions. NLGI3 lithium-based grease is used as the lubricant, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is employed as the numerical analysis method. The volume of fluid (VOF) is used to kinematically describe the flow field, and the distribution of grease under different speed conditions is obtained through computer numerical simulation and visualization processing. The results indicate that under high-speed conditions, the proportion of grease distribution on the outer raceway is greater than that on the inner raceway. As the speed increases, the pressure of the grease oil film decreases, and the film thickness increases.

articleTitle: Bayesian Deep Learning Framework with Variational Inference for Uncertainty Quantification in RUL Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Uncertainty in Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction must be quantified to provide confidence in the results. Balancing the quantification of uncertainty with the need for accurate predictions is a challenge. To this end, this paper presents a novel Bayesian Deep Learning (BDL) method with Variational Inference (VI) for predicting the RUL of mechanical equipment and quantifying the associated uncertainty. The proposed framework introduces a new Evidence Lower Bound (ELBO) loss function, controlling the trade-off between the negative log-likelihood loss and the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence via a tunable weight parameter. The proposed approach integrates a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to effectively handle sequential sensory data, and enhances prediction accuracy by incorporating attention mechanism that emphasizes critical time steps. A case study utilizing a turbofan engine dataset demonstrates the superiority of this method, achieving lower Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) compared to other Bayesian approaches.

articleTitle: Advanced Remaining Useful Life of Lithium-Ion Batteries Prediction with Positive and Negative Perceptron and Convolution Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) play a significant role in various applications such as electric vehicles, portable electronic devices, and renewable energy storage systems. Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of LIBs is essential for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of battery management systems and establishing optimal maintenance plans. In this study, we propose the deep learning network with positive and negative perceptron and convolution neural network (DNPC) that combines the positive and negative perceptron (PNC) model and the convolution neural network (CNN) model, which have high prediction accuracy for the RUL of LIBs. Experimental results using the LIBs dataset show that the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for the RUL prediction using test dataset of DNPC are 98.86 [cycle] and 7.25%, respectively, which are lower compared to other deep learning networks (DNNs). Both RMSE and MAPE of the DNPC are also lower compared to other studies using the same LIBs dataset. When analyzing the combination results of the PNC model with other models, the DNN combining the PNC model with the LSTM model has higher RMSE and MAPE, whereas the DNN using the PNC model alone has lower RMSE and MAPE. This means that while the PNC model is suitable for prediction RUL of LIBs, its effectiveness may decrease when combined with recurrent neural network (RNN)-based models. Future research aims to develop a new deep learning model that can enhance synergy with the PNC model and validate their usefulness across various battery types and industrial fields.

articleTitle: Stress Sensitivity Analysis of Grating Encoders Based on Accelerated Degradation Test
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: To obtain the effect of temperature, humidity and vibration on the life of grating encoder. This paper proposes a stress sensitivity analysis method for grating encoder based on accelerated degradation test. Firstly, the method of constructing the three-stress accelerated degradation test bench of the grating encoder is given, which realizes the loading and control of temperature, humidity and vibration and the collection of performance degradation data. Secondly, the stress sensitivity analysis method of grating encoder is proposed based on the accelerated degradation model. Based on the rated working conditions, the sensitivity analysis of the three accelerated stresses is carried out, and the relationship between the change of stress level and the lifetime is obtained. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a case study.

articleTitle: Home Appliance Reliability Study – The Failure of the Turntable Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This document has the purpose to present a new reliability validation test procedure for turntable motor, based on innovative experimental outcomes. Design of Experiment principles have been used to implement a test plan and the outputs have been used to select the aging factors. Load profile has been derived considering the results of a survey about the cooking habits. The failure mode under study has been characterized and replicated playing with the environmental conditions. Acceleration factors has been calculated using Reliasoft®. A new way to evaluate the stress distribution, enhanced the Stress-Strength analysis that provides the failure probability calculation. The new validation test procedure proposed is a demonstration test based on Lognormal distribution.

articleTitle: Quantum Physics Stochastic Neural Networks (QPNN)
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In this paper we introduce a framework of Quantum Probability (QP) as a generalized probability theory under limited information. We show that the proposed QP includes the Classical Probability (CP) as a particular case. Moreover, QP is linked to the classical mechanics through the concepts of action, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian. Starting from our QP formalism we sketch the formulation of Quantum Physics Neural Networks (QPNN) able to take into account limited information and model uncertainty. Relations with statistical physics and Ising model, Reduced Boltzmann Machines (RBM) and Deep Belief Networks (DBN) are discussed. It is also discussed their connection with Quantum Imprecise Bayesian Network (QIBN), recently proposed for sustainability and resilience of socio-ecological technical systems under uncertainty.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Analysis for Battery Health State Based on Bat Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Online estimation of the state of health (SOH) is critical to the safe and stable operation of battery management systems (BMS), which improve energy utilization and ensure battery safety. Therefore, we propose a new algorithm—Kernel Extreme Learning Machine(SOH) based on Bat Algorithm(BA) optimization—which combines BA and SOH. At the same time, considering the existence of uncertain parameters in the data set, the universal grey system theory is used to predict the SOH. The simulation results show that the BA provides the optimal solution of hyper-parameters for the KELM, improves the precision of the model and reduces its complexity. The feasibility of this method is proved by the SOH estimation of four different types of batteries.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling of CNC Machine Tool Electric Spindle Based on Environmental Factors
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Accurate reliability evaluation of CNC machine tool electric spindles is often challenged by a lack of fault data. This paper proposes a novel approach using a two-parameter Weibull distribution model that integrates environmental factors to address this issue. Unlike traditional models, our method combines expert judgment and historical product data with the concept of environmental factors, providing a more robust evaluation of electric spindle reliability, especially under small sample conditions. The mean time between failures (MTBF) is used as the evaluation index, and we derive the posterior distribution of Weibull parameters using Bayesian theory. This approach allows for a comprehensive reliability model that accounts for varying operating conditions. Our results demonstrate that incorporating environmental factors leads to a more accurate and reliable assessment of CNC machine tool electric spindles, offering a new theoretical and practical basis for reliability evaluation in similar mechanical products.

articleTitle: Redundancy Analysis of Multi-State Systems with Common Bus Performance Sharing
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Multi-state systems (MSSs) with common bus performance sharing (CBPS) is widely exist in practical engineering. This system is a typical redundant system to ensure the reliable operation. It considers two MSSs connected via a common bus, either of which has to satisfy its own demands, then transfer performance to the other system in order to improve the whole system reliability. In this paper, a new reliability model for MSSs with CBPS is proposed. Each multi-state component has a random performance and random demand. A Markov model is established to describe the performance and demand variations. An algorithm based on the universal generating function (UGF) method is proposed to evaluate the reliability of the whole system. The sensitivity analysis of systems with a given transmission capacity is discussed. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the method is illustrated by a numerical example.

articleTitle: A Black-Box Time-Discretization Scheme for Time-Dependent Reliability Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: We propose a time-discretization scheme for time-dependent reliability problems. It takes a general, “black-box” limit-state function (LSF) with a fine temporal mesh and a small number of realizations, and reduces the temporal discretization to a few critical time instants where failure is more likely to take place. No assumption is made about the underlying structure of the auto-covariance function of the LSF as an stochastic process, rather, the correlation structure is empirically estimated and exploited to reduce redundant information. The scheme is a first step in the development of general time-discretization procedures that can be combined with active-learning strategies and surrogate reliability to tackle complex time-dependent reliability problems. Two representative problems are solved, with crude MCS, to illustrate the concept and show the consistency of results.

articleTitle: Taxonomy of Safe Uncertainty Handling in the Context of Dynamic Risk Management
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Autonomous systems bear great potential to provide a multitude of benefits for society. In this context, the term utility describes the system's usefulness. Due to uncertainty related to the operating conditions as well as the utilised technologies, providing high utility and simultaneously ensuring safety is often contradictory. Due to imprecise risk assessments, systems might operate more conservatively even though the situation permits more permissive control approaches. Dynamic Risk Management (DRM) addresses this issue through the continuous monitoring of the system's operating context in order to optimise utility while simultaneously ensuring safety. This work advances the state-of -the-art by classifying the spectrum of DRM schemes in the dimensions of utility and assurability. The ability of a system to provide precise and trustworthy uncertainty estimates is thereby identified as major factor to improve utility.

articleTitle: Application of Cumulative Exposure Model for the Step-Up Voltage Tests of MOSFET Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This article examines the Weibull Cumulative Exposure (CE) model and its application to voltage breakdown data of MOSFET devices in multi-step step-stress accelerated life tests. The model uses an inverse power law function to depict the lifetime dependency on the applied gate voltage needed for a MOSFET device to breakdown. Additionally, a mixture model is employed to distinguish between two failure modes: “intrinsic” and “extrinsic”. The results show that this approach allows for the characterization of two different types of MOSFET devices, namely planar and trench, and provides failure probabilities for different failure modes. This information is valuable for accurately evaluating the quality and reliability of MOSFET devices.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Asset Management in Oil & Gas Recovery Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Field Development Planning (FDP) for oil and gas (O&G) recovery projects requires strategic well placement and infrastructure design to maximize hydrocarbon extraction. This work presents a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework based on Deep Q-Networks (DQN) for the optimization of drilling scheduling. Different sets of parameters describing the reservoir characteristics are considered for the definition of the state space and the parameter combination providing the largest profit over the entire lifetime of the oil project is identified. The proposed framework is validated considering a synthetic case study that emulates the complexity of the drilling scheduling problem in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis and Evaluation of the Design of Bifurcation Tunnel Diverting and Merging Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: With the increasing demand for road construction and limited land use on the ground, the bifurcation tunnel interchange project will become a common engineering form for future tight road networks. The safety of the branching and merging areas in tunnels should be given attention due to the influence of tunnel structures. By analyzing the driving characteristics of vehicles in the branching tunnel merging area, based on the visual distance requirements and vehicle driving characteristics of the merging area, the merging area and design reliability requirements of the branching tunnel were proposed. A reliability judgment model for the splitting impact based on the secondary deceleration theory was constructed, and reliability judgment standards for the length design of parallel deceleration lanes and direct deceleration lanes in the branching tunnel were proposed. This provides some reference and guidance for the design engineering practice and research of the branching tunnel merging area in the future.

articleTitle: Reliability Modeling and Analysis of Lithium-Ion Battery Packs in Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Renewable energy systems (RES) are emerging as clean power systems. Battery pack is one of the most critical components in RES. Since the power generation and load of RES is time-varying, it is essential to conduct credible reliability analysis of battery packs according to application scenarios. In this study, a belief reliability model for lithium-ion battery packs is developed based on the reliability science principles, taking into account functional requirements, battery degradation, and various sources of uncertainties. Firstly, the state of charge (SOC) of the battery pack is identified as the key performance indicator according to functional requirements. Next, an equivalent circuit model (ECM) is utilized and a cell-to-pack model is constructed to establish the performance margin model. Furthermore, the battery capacity loss over time is considered. Afterwards, the sources of uncertainties are analyzed and quantified with the help of probability theory. Ultimately, the reliability model is established. A case study of a battery pack in RES is introduced to show the effectiveness of the proposed model. The findings indicate that the proposed model can assess the reliability of the battery pack based on internal parameters and operating profiles, aligning closely with its functional requirements. Additionally, guidance can be provided for designers to achieve high reliability standards.

articleTitle: Enhancing Safety of Power Supply Systems in Automotive Applications: Integrating Functional Safety (FuSa) and Safety of the Intended Functionality (SOTIF)
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The automotive industry's development towards electrification and automation raises special attention to Safety-Related Availability (SaRA) of onboard power supply systems (powernets). This paper provides insights into the current state of safety development for powernets and highlights the challenges in the safety argumentation for batteries. Our key contributions are twofold: First, we synchronize FuSa and SOTIF safety processes to manage intricate interactions and enhance reusability. We present a case study demonstrating how this integrated process is applied to powernets. Second, we extend the application of SOTIF to low-level complex safety measures, such as battery diagnosis, as a supplement to the high-level functional safety concept. We further discuss the applicability of SOTIF to battery diagnosis and specifically focus on deriving acceptance criteria, identifying functional insufficiencies, defining triggering conditions, and comparing various validation methods. Despite the differences from AD/ADAS, SOTIF's goal to mitigate potential risks resulting from functional insufficiencies remains applicable to battery diagnosis. Finally, we propose a safety validation framework combining sensitivity analysis, probabilistic surrogate models, and importance sampling to provide quantitative safety argumentation. This paper primarily focuses on theoretical analysis and is intended to lay a robust theoretical foundation for power supply safety.

articleTitle: Software-Based Fault Tolerance with Arithmetic Coding for Floating-Points
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Arithmetic coding, also known as encoded or coded processing, is a software-based fault-tolerance approach that detects hardware faults at the software level by exploiting information redundancy. Existing arithmetic coding focuses on integer arithmetic. However, the increasing complexity of safety functions, e.g. from industrial robotics, requires floating-point arithmetic. This paper shows the challenges of applying existing integer codes to floating-point numbers. We identify and compare existing approaches from literature and new approaches in this paper. The comparison includes an analysis of performance, fault detection capability, hardware reliability, constraints on algorithm development, and accuracy.

articleTitle: Modeling and Verification of Identity Authentication Protocols in Cloud-Edge-End Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: The digital transformation of power systems, leveraging cloud-edge-end architectures, is key to smart industry evolution. However, escalating security threats highlight the urgent need for rigorous identity authentication protocol verification. The growing traffic and user expectations necessitate real-time, lightweight authentication solutions, prompting the creation of innovative security measures. In this paper, we employ formal methods to rigorously assess novel security protocols within power system's cloud-edge-end architecture, focusing on their correctness and security. It begins with a thorough analysis of the architecture's constituents: edge computing resources, devices, and network connections. A formal approach utilizing High-Level Protocol Specification Language (HLPSL) is then introduced to detail the new identity authentication protocol, addressing access control, authentication, and encryption. The protocol undergoes formal verification via AVISPA, employing model checking to confirm adherence to specific security properties. This process aids in uncovering potential risks and vulnerabilities, reinforcing the power system's security. The thorough validation of the protocol's security attributes guarantees its capability to meet the evolving security requirements of the cloud-edge-end environment, fortifying system resilience amidst ongoing digital advancements and cybersecurity threats.

articleTitle: Reliability-Based Topology Optimization of Reinforced Composite Shell
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In this paper, a reliability-based topology optimization (RBTO) approach is introduced for a composite shell. The RBTO method is divided into deterministic topology optimization and uncertainty analysis by decoupled strategy. It employs the bi-directional evolutionary structural optimization (BESO) algorithm, based on a composite material interpolation model, for solving deterministic topology optimization. During uncertainty analysis, the performance measure approach (PMA) is used to convert probabilistic constraints into probabilistic performance measures, thereby avoiding multiple integral failure probability. Uncertainty propagation is then carried out using the response surface method (RSM) based on the Hermite orthogonal polynomials. With the derivatives of the performance function to random variables, the most probable point (MPP) search is conducted using the enhanced hybrid mean value (EHMV) method. The paper concludes with a demonstration of the validity of the RBTO methodology through its application to the reinforced composite shell.

articleTitle: Belief Reliability Analysis Under the Parameter Uncertainty of Performance Margin Using Uncertain Random Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Belief reliability is a reliability metric considering both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty based on probability theory, uncertainty theory and chance theory. Generally, the belief reliability analysis process is conducted through the performance margin model of a system or a component. To model the parameters affected by different types of uncertainty in the margin model, in this paper, we describe them as random variables if they are mainly affected by aleatory uncertainty or uncertain variables if they contain mainly epistemic uncertainty. Based on this, a basic belief reliability model is first proposed according to the operational laws of chance theory. Since it is usually difficult to calculate the belief reliability analytically using this model, we also develop an uncertain random simulation method to cope with this problem based on the geometric properties of uncertainty theory. As an illustration, a case study of belief reliability analysis for an aero-hydraulic spool valve is performed.

articleTitle: Review and Comparison of Evaluation Indicators Based on Support Vector Machine Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Support Vector Machine (SVM) is a widely-used supervised learning algorithm with extensive applications in classification problems. It is crucial to use appropriate evaluation metrics to assess the performance of SVM classification models. This article reviews and compares commonly used SVM classification evaluation indicators, including accuracy, precision, recall, Fl score, ROC curve, and AUC value. The comparison of classification results using these indicators shows variation across different datasets. Thoughtful selection of appropriate evaluation indicators is essential for accurate model evaluation. This research can assist researchers and practitioners in choosing an optimal number of datasets for a more precise evaluation of SVM classification model performance.

Index Terms: Area Under Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articleTitle: Safe Vehicular Platooning Control: Mitigating Uncertainty and Enhancing Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: This paper explores a safe control strategy for autonomous vehicle platooning, focusing on mitigating the effects of uncertainty and maintaining platoon stability. Autonomous platooning, enabled by vehicle-to-everything communication, is critical in intelligent transportation systems to enhance safety, reduce fuel consumption, and minimize traffic delays. However, real-world conditions such as communication delays, external disturbances, and vehicle inconsistencies can introduce instability. This study presents a control algorithm that manages inter-vehicle distance through dynamic speed adjustment and string stability criteria. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method under varying levels of external disturbances, demonstrating its ability to maintain desired distance gap and prevent amplification of disturbances within the platoon.

articleTitle: Common Cause Failure Assessment Suitable for a System on a Chip Design According to ISO 13849 Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Common cause failures are an important part of the risk and reliability assessment of an integrated circuit. Since it is often impossible to guarantee the full separation of redundant channels implemented in the same System on Chip, in fail-safe operation, mitigation measures are also required within the integrated circuit to control (not only to avoid) the CCF, to reduce the overall risk. Following this approach an alternative approach to the CCF assessment methodology of ISO 13849 Annex F is proposed.

articleTitle: A Review of Uncertainty Management in Vehicular Platooning: Safety and Efficiency in Opportunistic Transport Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: In recent years, vehicular platooning systems have gained significant attention due to their potential to enhance road safety, fuel efficiency, and traffic flow. However, these systems face several challenges, including external disturbances, communication uncertainties, cyber-attacks, and heterogeneous vehicle dynamics. This paper presents a comprehensive review of state-of-the-art control strategies designed to address these challenges in vehicular platooning systems. The focus is on various control approaches such as adaptive control, model predictive control, and robust control, which offer solutions for maintaining platoon stability despite disturbances and communication failures. We also discuss event-triggered mechanisms, which aim to reduce communication load, and cybersecurity-focused protocols that protect platooning systems from attacks. A comparison of these strategies is presented based on several criteria. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research directions to improve the robustness and real-time applicability of vehicular platooning systems in increasingly dynamic and uncertain environments.

articleTitle: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Method for Finding the Risk-Based Optimal Prescriptive Maintenance Policy of Degrading Safety Barriers
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Safety barriers have to be properly maintained to limit the reduction of their performance due to age. In this work, we formulate the problem of finding the optimal maintenance actions to be performed on the safety barriers as a Sequential Decision Problem (SDP). The SDP is, then, solved by Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), with Imitation Learning (IL) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). The resulting prescriptive maintenance policy accounts for the effects that the different maintenance actions have on the limitation of the degradation of the safety barriers and, ultimately, on the risk due to the escalation of the accidental scenarios. The novelty of the work lies in the formulation and efficient solution of the problem of risk-based prescriptive maintenance optimization for safety barriers, accounting for their age-dependent degradation. An application is shown with regards to a chemical facility exposed to Natural hazard-induced Technological (NaTech) risk, such as that due to earthquakes, and equipped with safety barriers whose performance degrades in time. The optimal prescriptive maintenance policy found by DRL is proven to outperform the typical maintenance strategy both in terms of cost and risk reduction.

articleTitle: A DBN-Based Time Analysis Method for Emergency Response Considering Mental Workload and Fatigue
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Emergency response can assist operators to prevent the escalation of incidents, while it must be successfully completed within the specified time. Therefore, it is essential to analyze the response time of the emergency response. Fatigue, an important factor affecting response time, can extend personnel response time and reduce response efficiency. Meanwhile, the accumulation speed of fatigue increases with the increase of mental workload. This paper proposes a Dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN)-based time analysis method to predict cumulative response times for emergency response tasks, and considers the effects of mental workload and fatigue. The method introduces a fatigue model based on the Multiple Resource Theory (MRT) to analyze the effect of mental workload on the accumulation speed of fatigue, as well as a response time model that takes into account the uncertainty of personnel behavior to analyze the effect of fatigue on response time. This paper demonstrates the application of the method in analyzing the man overboard emergency response.

articleTitle: Enhancing a Soft GPU IP Reliability Against SEUs in Space: Modelling Approach and Criticality Analysis on a Radiation-Tolerant FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Field Programmable Gate Arrays find extensive use across various domains, ranging from telecommunications to Machine Learning tasks. In the context of space applications, they emerge as a highly favourable choice, owing to their high degree of flexibility and their accessibility in different silicon-grade technologies. However, due to the high associated costs of radiation-hardened devices, the prevalence of radiation-tolerant devices is more common in practical deployment scenarios. In this sense, robustness-enhancing techniques can still be applied, thus allowing the employment of these devices in long-duration tasks without the need for a radiation-hardened counterpart. In this paper, we propose a modelling approach for estimating the reliability of a digital design system in space before carrying out fault injection tests and radiation campaigns. For this purpose, we employ a high-level tool called Mobius to obtain a first reliability estimation against Single Event Upsets by means of Fault Tree Models. We also propose a novel methodology for defining which fault mitigation techniques should be applied to each design sub-module, considering the most commonly used in the space environment. In particular, we focus on a specific use case, namely a Soft Graphic Processing Unit IP, implemented on the Xilinx RT XQRKU060 FPGA. We analyze the criticality, power and area impact of the most important design parts of the GPU when implemented in hardware, introducing a classification approach for associating an appropriate fault mitigation technique with each of them. Finally, in the last section of the paper, we hint at future development and conclude the work.

articleTitle: Providing Complete High-Level Overviews of Hospital Resilience Through Semi-Quantitative Stress Tests
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Strengthening the resilience of hospital systems has gained significant attention following the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing global conflicts, which have highlighted their vulnerability to potentially disruptive events. This paper presents a novel approach to provide complete high-level overviews of hospital resilience through semi-quantitative stress tests. The paper describes the theoretical framework and a tool which facilitates its implementation. Additionally, the approach is demonstrated by using it to assess the resilience of a hospital in Lebanon. It is shown that the quantification of resilience through specific service measures enables clear identification of where changes to the hospital system can improve hospital resilience, as well as the possible magnitude of resilience improvement. The approach uses a relatively short list of indicators to help balance comprehensiveness and computational efficiency. An example of a potentially disruptive event, i.e., a stress test, is a mass casualty incident. The connection between the event and the service measures was developed semi-quantitatively using considerable information from scientific literature and expert opinion. Although the case study only consists of one stress test it demonstrates that this approach has considerable potential to provide a much-needed overview of the resilience of hospital systems and how the resilience can be best improved. Its use will provide valuable insights for both hospital managers and regulatory bodies in their discussions of how to best improve healthcare infrastructure.

articleTitle: Unravelling Safety-Critical Situations in Remote Operation Mode for Automated Trains - A Systematic Approach with STPA
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Automation is increasingly becoming an integral part of mainline rail operations. However, there are still significant challenges to be overcome on the way to fully automated mainline operations (grade of automation 4, GoA4). Ensuring safety in all GoA4 operational scenarios is paramount. By employing System-Theoretic Process Analysis (STPA), this paper aims to systematically analyse the control structures and processes of remote operation mode in fully automated railway operations to derive potential safety risks. By identifying and addressing safety-critical situations, railway operators can enhance the reliability, efficiency, and safety of fully automated railway systems by mitigating the reasons for safety-critical situations before the system migration. In fully automated railway operations, where various subsystems and components interact dynamically, understanding these systemic relationships is crucial for identifying safety-critical situations. STPA considers the interactions and dependencies between the system components within the system architecture and allows to identify hazards from the point of operational view (systemic view). In this paper, 11 safety-critical situations occurring during remote operation mode of automated trains could be identified using STPA. Additionally to the identified safety-critical situations, possible architectural and operational safety measures are presented.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in Hybrid-Fiber Coaxial Networks Using Sliding Window-Based Features
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on System Reliability and Safety (ICSRS)
abstract: Proactive Network Maintenance (PNM) is a cornerstone for cable network reliability. Accurate fault detection and diagnosis of faults in hybrid-fiber coaxial (HFC) networks are significant for providing customers high service quality, optimizing network operations and minimizing related costs.
